summary: The Bank of England announced the framework for its 2025 Bank Capital Stress Test, which will assess the resilience of the UK banking system against a severe but plausible tail-risk scenario featuring deep simultaneous recessions in the UK and global economies, large falls in asset prices, higher global interest rates, and stressed misconduct costs. Seven banking groups representing 75% of UK lending will participate. The test is the successor to the annual cyclical scenario under the previous approach and the first since the end of IFRS 9 transitional arrangements. Results will be published in Q4 2025 and will inform capital buffer settings.
why_it_matters: The stress test framework directly affects capital requirements for major UK banks, influencing their capacity to absorb shocks and continue lending during economic downturns. Results will shape Prudential Regulation Authority buffer calibrations and broader financial stability assessments. The first post-IFRS 9 transitional test - changes to calibration were implemented to maintain unchanged risk tolerance.
macro_context: The scenario is countercyclical, designed to test resilience during periods of elevated vulnerability. It features a severe negative global supply shock with geopolitical tensions driving commodity price increases, supply chain disruptions, sharp inflation rises, and central bank rate increases. Government bond yields in advanced economies rise. This differs from Monetary Policy Committee forecast scenarios.
market_structure_context: Seven banking groups participate at the highest UK consolidation level, representing 75% of lending to the UK real economy. The Bank is not requesting standalone submissions from ring-fenced subgroups in this test cycle. Results will be published at both aggregate and individual bank levels for transparency and market discipline.
